newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money market rates edge up,no rate rise seen.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money market rates edge up,no rate rise seen.

text.p: Dutch money market rates rose fractionally on Thursday, but dealers said they did not yet expect a rise in the special advances rate when the central bank sets a new pact at 1400 GMT.
"A rate rise is not impossible, but it is more likely the Nederlandsche Bank would wait for Germany first to make such a move," said one dealer.
He said any move would would probably involve more than just a rise of the special advances rate.
"The secured loans would probably be raised by 25 basis points as well," the dealer said.
Dealers said rates were likely to move up slowly because traders were nervous. "Inflation is gradually moving up, and investors in the share market are getting nervous," said another dealer.
Call money rates were bid between 3.25 and 3.31 percent versus a range between 3.18 and 3.25 on Wednesday.
Three months deposits rose two basis points to 3.36 percent bid.
The guilder was slightly stronger at 112.65 per 100 marks compared to 112.66 on Wednesday.
